title: Misleading Pricing, Unauthorized Coin Deduction, and Three Days of Customer Service Runaround
body: I enjoyed the story I was reading on this app, but my experience with its purchasing system and customer service has made me unwilling to spend any more money here. My complaint is very specific. I was reading Married the Prince While Pregnant. Before recharging my account, Chapter 250 was displayed at 210 coins. I purchased additional coins based on the price being shown. After the recharge, however, the app deducted 500 coins for Chapter 250. I was not shown a 500-coin price and asked to approve it before the deduction, nor did I knowingly authorize a 500-coin purchase. I contacted customer service and requested a refund of the 290-coin difference. What should have been a straightforward transaction dispute turned into three days of repeatedly explaining the same issue. Customer service initially responded about subscriptions and recurring billing, even though I repeatedly explained that I did not have a subscription and was disputing a specific chapter transaction. I was then told their technical team was reviewing my account. Later, I was told that sneak-preview chapters cost more than regular chapters. That still did not address my complaint. I never disputed their right to charge 500 coins for an early-access chapter. I disputed displaying one price and then deducting a different amount without presenting that amount to me for approval. Support eventually confirmed that 500 coins were deducted for Chapter 250 of Married the Prince While Pregnant. They then suggested that if the chapter unlocked automatically, I should turn off the auto-unlock feature. That explanation created another problem. I checked the app and documented the settings. “Auto-unlock following unpurchased chapters” is OFF. I also documented the purchase screen for Chapter 251, which clearly displays the price, in this case 50 coins, and provides an “Unlock Current Chapter” button before the transaction. That is exactly the type of price disclosure and affirmative purchase process that should have occurred before 500 coins were deducted for Chapter 250. Even more frustrating, after support had already identified the exact book and chapter in writing, I was later asked to provide the book title again so they could investigate Chapter 250. The title was already throughout the conversation, and their own representative had previously identified it. After three days, I still did not receive a direct resolution to the original question: Are you refunding the disputed 290 coins or not? At that point, I requested a refund of my full $49.99 purchase rather than continue going in circles. My concern is not that different chapters have different prices. My concern is transaction transparency and authorization. If a chapter costs 500 coins, display 500 coins and allow the customer to decide whether to purchase it. If the displayed price changes after a customer recharges, show the new price and obtain confirmation before deducting the coins. Customers should not have to spend days arguing with customer service just to determine why an amount different from the displayed price was deducted from their account. The stories may be entertaining, but based on my experience with the purchasing system and the way this dispute has been handled, I cannot recommend spending money on this app.

title: Maybe
body: I began reading a book that had (470 ?) chapters. I don’t mind the length of the book, but a chapter should be longer than a page and a half. The basic story is interesting, and there’s grammar and spelling are perfect, but there’s so much superfluous and repetitive dialog and description that it becomes boring. Everybody wants to kill everyone else. This book could use a decent proof reader. Character names change for a few chapters, suggesting that chapters weren’t written sequentially, and the final writing renamed characters. Just missed a few chapters. But the reader has to figure out Who is who so that the plot makes some sense. There are lots of family members in all of the families. A family tree design would help the readers a lot, especially those that put down a book for a day or two. And the repetition…every woman in the book makes a fist so tight that her fingernails draw blood. There’s more, but you get the idea. The geography…I know the author is from another country, but if I wrote a book that described a city park in Beijing that had giant redwoods, you’d think I hadn’t done my homework. Redwoods don’t grow on the east coast. They’re west coast trees. And the Appalachian mountains are pretty short. The highest peak is just over 6,600 ft. And then there’s poor Jeremiah. He never eats, he never sleeps, heck, he never even takes a shower. Is he a robot? I finally gave up after 390+ chapters.

title: DON’T WASTE YOUR TIME!!!
body: I’m giving 5 stars only so people will see. Do not get this app!! You watch endless amounts of adds for a few coins in order to read unless you want to buy expensive coins and spend probably $100 for one book. There are limited times and ways to earn coins. One way you watch 3 adds to unlock 1 short chapter and that’s only offered for a maximum of 3 per day. I have watched 25 adds just to get 25 coins! Don’t bother with earning points by adds which are supposed to convert to coins. I watched tons of adds to build them up but they only convert a few at a time once per day. Then you get stuck with no choice unable to read and I refuse to watch more adds earning them tons of money! I found the book I was reading on MegaNovel which at least always allows an option of watching one add to continue reading. Much simpler! Also search Kindle where you can purchase for a small amount if it’s available there. Hope this helps someone.
